guards: a Rails change with SQL built from params, an admin check that skips destroy, mass assignment of every attribute and a callback that runs on every save is reviewed as Rails code
amended: Copied from ../cases/rails-controller-model.json on 2026-10-08 to score this run with the scorer that needs words on every plant: each plant and side issue that had no mentions got them; no other field changed.

bugs.truth: params[:q] is put into the SQL string of where, so a caller can run any SQL. The fix is a bound value: where("email LIKE ?", "%#{User.sanitize_sql_like(params[:q])}%").
destroy is added to the actions that skip require_admin, so any user with a token can delete any user. The fix is to leave destroy out of except.
permit! allows every attribute, so a request can set admin or api_token on a user. The fix is to permit the editable attributes by name, such as permit(:email).
after_save runs on every update, so a user gets the welcome email again each time their record changes. The fix is after_create_commit.
